title.zh: 卷一百五十 志第一百〇三 輿服二
title.raw: 卷一百五十 志第一百〇三 輿服二 Volume 150 Treatises 103: Carriages and Clothes 2

sentences.zh: 輿服二○后妃車輿皇太子王公以下車輿傘扇鞍勒門戟旌節。

translations.literal: Carriages and Attire 2: empress and consort carriages; crown prince; princes and nobles of rank and below — their carriages; parasols and fans; saddles and bridles; gate halberds; banners and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Attire, Part 2: the carriages of empresses and consorts, of the crown prince, and of imperial princes and officials down through the ranks; parasols and fans; saddles and bridles; gate halberds; banners; and ceremonial staffs.

sentences.zh: 皇后之車，唐制六等：一曰重翟，二曰厭翟，三曰翟車，四曰安車，五曰四望車，六曰金根車。

translations.literal: The empress's carriages: under the Tang system there were six grades — first, the Heavy Pheasant carriage; second, the Fulfilled Pheasant carriage; third, the Pheasant carriage; fourth, the Peace carriage; fifth, the Four-Views carriage; sixth, the Golden Root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The empress rode in carriages ranked in six grades under Tang regulations: the Heavy Pheasant, the Fulfilled Pheasant, the Pheasant, the Peace, the Four-Views, and the Golden Root carriages.

sentences.zh: 宋因之，初用厭翟車。

translations.literal: The Song followed this system, at first using the Fulfilled Pheasant carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Song adopted the same arrangement and initially used the Fulfilled Pheasant carriage.

sentences.zh: 其制：箱上有平盤，四角曲闌，兩壁紗窗，龜文，金鳳翅，前有虛匱、香爐、香寶，緋繡幰衣、絡帶、門簾，三轅鳳首，畫梯，推竿，行馬，緋繒裹索。

translations.literal: Its specifications: atop the box was a level platform; curved balustrades at the four corners; gauze windows on both sides with tortoise-pattern ornament and golden phoenix wings; in front were empty caskets, incense censers, and incense boxes; scarlet embroidered canopy robes, net belts, and door curtains; three shafts with phoenix heads; painted ladders, pushing poles, and running boards; scarlet silk wrapping the ropes.
translations.idiomatic: It was built as follows: a flat platform on the carriage box, curved railings at each corner, gauze-paneled side walls with tortoise motifs and golden phoenix wings, censers and incense boxes mounted in front, scarlet embroidered canopies, net belts, and door curtains, three phoenix-headed shafts, painted ladders and pushing poles with running boards, and scarlet silk cords binding the harness.

sentences.zh: 駕六馬，金銅麵，纓轡，鈴攀，緋屜。

translations.literal: It was drawn by six horses with gilt-bronze face ornaments, tassels and bridles, bell pendants, and scarlet knee covers.
translations.idiomatic: Six horses drew it, fitted with gilt-bronze brow plates, tasseled bridles, bell pendants, and scarlet knee covers.

sentences.zh: 駕士三十人，武弁、緋繡衫。

translations.literal: Thirty carriage attendants wore military caps and scarlet embroidered jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty attendants, in military caps and scarlet embroidered jackets, walked beside it.

sentences.zh: 常出止用正、副金塗銀裝白藤輿各一，上覆棕櫚屋，飾以鳳，輦官服同乘輿平頭輦之制。

translations.literal: For ordinary outings only one principal and one secondary white-rattan palanquin with gold-over-silver fittings were used, each topped with a palm-thatch canopy decorated with phoenixes; the attire of palanquin officers followed the regulations for the imperial flat-topped palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: On routine outings she used only a principal and a secondary white-rattan palanquin with gold-over-silver fittings, each covered by a palm-thatch canopy adorned with phoenixes; the palanquin bearers dressed as prescribed for the imperial flat-topped palanquin.

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和三年，議禮局上皇后車輿之制：重翟車，青質，金飾諸末，間以五采。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Zhenghe reign of Emperor Huizong, the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual presented the regulations for the empress's carriages: the Heavy Pheasant carriage was of green material, with gold ornament on all extremities, interspersed with the five colors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113, during Emperor Huizong's Zhenghe reign, the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual submitted regulations for the empress's carriages: the Heavy Pheasant carriage was green-bodied, gilt at every extremity, and set off with the five colors.

sentences.zh: 輪金根朱牙。

translations.literal: The wheels had golden hubs and vermilion spokes.
translations.idiomatic: Its wheels had golden hubs and vermilion spokes.

sentences.zh: 其箱飾以重翟羽，四面施雲鳳、孔雀，刻鏤龜文。

translations.literal: The box was adorned with heavy pheasant feathers; on all four sides were cloud-phoenixes and peacocks, with tortoise patterns carved in relief.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage box was trimmed with heavy pheasant plumes, cloud-phoenixes and peacocks on all four sides, and tortoise motifs carved in relief.

sentences.zh: 頂輪上施金立鳳、耀葉。

translations.literal: On the crown of the wheel hub were set gilt standing phoenixes and radiant leaf ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Gilt standing phoenixes and radiant leaf ornaments crowned the wheel hubs.

sentences.zh: 青羅幰衣一，紫羅畫雲龍絡帶二，青絲絡網二，紫羅畫帷一，青羅畫雲龍夾幔二。

translations.literal: One green silk canopy robe; two purple silk net belts painted with cloud-dragons; two green silk net panels; one purple silk painted curtain; two green silk side curtains painted with cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: It carried one green silk canopy robe, two purple silk net belts painted with cloud-dragons, two green silk net panels, one purple silk painted curtain, and two green silk side curtains painted with cloud-dragons.

sentences.zh: 車內設紅褥及坐，橫轅上施立鳳八。

translations.literal: Inside the carriage were a red cushion and seat; on the cross-shaft were set eight standing phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Within were a red cushion and seat, and eight standing phoenixes mounted on the cross-shaft.

sentences.zh: 香匱設香爐、香寶，香匱飾以螭首。

translations.literal: The incense casket held an incense censer and incense boxes; the casket was ornamented with dragon heads.
translations.idiomatic: Its incense casket held censers and incense boxes and was ornamented with hornless-dragon heads.

sentences.zh: 前後施簾，長轅三，飾以鳳頭，青繒裹索。

translations.literal: Curtains were hung fore and aft; there were three long shafts ornamented with phoenix heads; green silk wrapped the ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains hung fore and aft; three long shafts bore phoenix-head ornaments, and green silk wrapped the harness ropes.

sentences.zh: 駕青馬六，馬有銅麵，插翟羽，鞶纓，攀胸鈴拂，青屜，青包尾。

translations.literal: Six green horses drew it; each horse had a bronze face plate, pheasant feathers inserted, belly bands and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, green knee covers, and green tail wrappers.
translations.idiomatic: Six green horses drew it, each fitted with a bronze brow plate, inserted pheasant plumes, belly bands and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, green knee covers, and green tail wrappers.

sentences.zh: 若受冊、謁景靈宮，則乘之。

translations.literal: When receiving the investiture patent or paying homage at the Jingling Palace, she rode in this carriage.
translations.idiomatic: She rode in it when receiving her patent of investiture or when paying homage at the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 厭翟車，赤質，其箱飾以次翟羽；

translations.literal: The Fulfilled Pheasant carriage was of red material; its box was adorned with secondary pheasant feathers;
translations.idiomatic: The Fulfilled Pheasant carriage was red-bodied, its box trimmed with secondary pheasant plumes;

sentences.zh: 紫幰衣，紅絲絡網，紅羅畫絡帶，夾幔錦帷，餘如重翟車。

translations.literal: purple canopy robes, red silk net panels, red silk painted net belts, brocade side curtains and curtains — the rest as on the Heavy Pheasant carriage.
translations.idiomatic: with purple canopy robes, red silk net panels, painted red silk net belts, brocade side curtains and curtains, and otherwise as on the Heavy Pheasant carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕赤騮四。

translations.literal: Four chestnut bays drew it.
translations.idiomatic: Four chestnut bays drew it.

sentences.zh: 若親蠶則乘之。

translations.literal: When personally tending the silkworms, she rode in it.
translations.idiomatic: She rode in it when personally tending the silkworms.

sentences.zh: 翟車，黃質，其車側飾以翟羽；

translations.literal: The Pheasant carriage was of yellow material; its sides were adorned with pheasant feathers;
translations.idiomatic: The Pheasant carriage was yellow-bodied, its sides trimmed with pheasant plumes;

sentences.zh: 黃幰衣，黃絲絡網，錦帷絡帶，餘如重翟車。

translations.literal: yellow canopy robes, yellow silk net panels, brocade curtains and net belts — the rest as on the Heavy Pheasant carriage.
translations.idiomatic: with yellow canopy robes, yellow silk net panels, brocade curtains and net belts, and otherwise as on the Heavy Pheasant carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕黃騮四。

translations.literal: Four yellow bays drew it.
translations.idiomatic: Four yellow bays drew it.

sentences.zh: 安車，赤質，金飾，間以五采，刻鏤龜文；

translations.literal: The Peace carriage was of red material, with gold ornament interspersed with the five colors and tortoise patterns carved in relief;
translations.idiomatic: The Peace carriage was red-bodied, gilt and set with the five colors, with tortoise motifs carved in relief;

sentences.zh: 紫幰衣，錦帷絡帶，紅絲絡網，前後施簾；

translations.literal: purple canopy robes, brocade curtains and net belts, red silk net panels, curtains hung fore and aft;
translations.idiomatic: with purple canopy robes, brocade curtains and net belts, red silk net panels, and curtains fore and aft;

sentences.zh: 車內設褥及坐，長轅三，飾以鳳頭，駕赤騮四。

translations.literal: inside were a cushion and seat; three long shafts ornamented with phoenix heads; four chestnut bays drew it.
translations.idiomatic: Within were a cushion and seat; three long shafts bore phoenix-head ornaments; four chestnut bays drew it.

sentences.zh: 凡駕馬鞶纓之飾，並從車質。

translations.literal: For all harness horses, the belly-band and tassel ornaments followed the color of the carriage body.
translations.idiomatic: On every carriage, the horses' belly bands and tassels matched the body color of the vehicle.

sentences.zh: 四望車，朱質，青幰衣，餘同安車。

translations.literal: The Four-Views carriage was of vermilion material with green canopy robes; the rest as on the Peace carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Four-Views carriage was vermilion-bodied with green canopy robes and otherwise matched the Peace carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕牛三。

translations.literal: Three oxen drew it.
translations.idiomatic: Three oxen drew it.

sentences.zh: 金根車，朱質，紫幰衣，餘同安車。

translations.literal: The Golden Root carriage was of vermilion material with purple canopy robes; the rest as on the Peace carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Root carriage was vermilion-bodied with purple canopy robes and otherwise matched the Peace carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕牛三。

translations.literal: Three oxen drew it.
translations.idiomatic: Three oxen drew it.

sentences.zh: 自重翟車以下，備鹵簿則皆以次陳設。

translations.literal: From the Heavy Pheasant carriage downward, when the full guard of honor was provided, all were arrayed in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: When the full guard of honor was mustered, the carriages from the Heavy Pheasant downward were all displayed in descending rank.

sentences.zh: 藤輿，金塗銀裝。

translations.literal: The rattan palanquin had gold-over-silver fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The rattan palanquin was fitted with gold-over-silver mountings.

sentences.zh: 上覆棕櫚屋，以龍飾，常行之儀則用之。

translations.literal: It was topped with a palm-thatch canopy decorated with dragons and was used for the routine procession.
translations.idiomatic: A palm-thatch canopy adorned with dragons covered it, and it served for everyday processions.

sentences.zh: 龍肩輿。

translations.literal: The Dragon Shoulder Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Shoulder Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 一名棕簷子，一名龍簷子，舁以二竿，故名簷子，南渡後所製也。

translations.literal: It was also called the Palm-Eave Palanquin and the Dragon-Eave Palanquin; because it was borne on two poles, it was called an eave-palanquin — a form devised after the southward relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Also known as the Palm-Eave and Dragon-Eave palanquins, it took its common name from the two carrying poles; this design was introduced after the court moved south.

sentences.zh: 東都，皇后備厭翟車，常乘則白藤輿。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital the empress kept a Fulfilled Pheasant carriage in readiness but ordinarily rode in a white-rattan palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital the empress maintained a Fulfilled Pheasant carriage for ceremony but usually traveled in a white-rattan palanquin.

sentences.zh: 中興，以太后用龍輿，後惟用簷子，示有所尊也。

translations.literal: After the Restoration the empress dowager used the dragon palanquin; afterward only the eave-palanquin was used, to show that someone stood above.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration the empress dowager rode the dragon palanquin; thereafter only the eave-palanquin was used for the empress, marking that one person stood above her in rank.

sentences.zh: 其制：方質，棕頂，施走脊龍四，走脊雲子六，朱漆紅黃藤織百花龍為障；

translations.literal: Its specifications: a square body, palm top, four ridge-running dragons and six ridge-running cloud medallions set upon it, vermilion lacquer and red-and-yellow rattan woven with hundred-flower dragons as screens;
translations.idiomatic: It was square-bodied with a palm-frond canopy, four ridge-running dragons and six cloud medallions along the ridge, and vermilion-lacquered red-and-yellow rattan screens woven with hundred-flower dragon patterns;

sentences.zh: 緋門簾、看窗簾，朱漆藤坐椅，踏子，紅羅裀褥，軟屏，夾幔。

translations.literal: scarlet door curtains and viewing-window curtains, vermilion-lacquered rattan seat and chair, footrests, red silk cushions and mats, soft screens, and side curtains.
translations.idiomatic: with scarlet door curtains and viewing-window curtains, vermilion-lacquered rattan seats and chairs, footrests, red silk cushions and mats, soft screens, and side curtains.

sentences.zh: 隆興二年正月，皇后受冊畢，擇日朝謁，有司具儀物，乞乘肩輿龍簷。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Longxing, after the empress had completed receiving the investiture patent and a day was chosen for the court audience, the responsible offices prepared the ritual objects and requested that she ride in the shoulder-borne dragon-eave palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In early 1164, after the empress received her patent of investiture and a day was set for her court audience, the responsible offices prepared the ritual gear and asked that she ride in the shoulder-borne dragon-eave palanquin.

sentences.zh: 製造所受給使臣尹肇發，納中宮金塗銀葉棕櫚、朱漆紅黃藤織百花龍枰子、碌牙壓貼、鏤金雕木腰花泥版龍簷子一乘。

translations.literal: The envoy Yin Zhao of the Manufactories Office who had received the commission delivered to the Inner Palace one dragon-eave palanquin with gold-over-silver palm leaves, vermilion lacquer, red-and-yellow rattan woven with hundred-flower dragons on the platform, jade-inlaid pressure strips, and waist-flower panels of carved gilt wood on clay backing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhao, an envoy of the Manufactories Office, delivered to the Inner Palace one dragon-eave palanquin fitted with gold-over-silver palm leaves, a vermilion-lacquered platform of red-and-yellow rattan woven with hundred-flower dragons, jade-inlaid pressure strips, and waist panels of carved gilt wood on clay backing.

sentences.zh: 金塗銀頂子，龍頭六，走脊龍四，走脊雲子六，貼絡龍四十，貼絡雲子三十，鐸子八，插拴坐龍四，環索全，鈸遮那一副，檀香龜背紅紗窗四扇，紅羅緣紅篸門簾一，瀝水全，看窗簾二，朱漆藤麵明金雕木龍頭椅一，腳踏一，紅線絛結一，朱漆小幾二，紅羅褥全，紅羅緣肩膊席褥一十六，係帶全，金塗銀鐵胎杆鞫四，魚鉤四，火踏一，朱漆梯盤全，朱漆衣匣二，金塗銅手把葉段拓叉二，金塗銅叉頭拖泥行馬二，金塗銀葉杠子二，紅茸匾絛四，紅羅夾軟屏風、夾幔各一，襯腳席褥、靠背坐褥及踏床各一，紅絹十字帕一，竿袋四，魚鉤帕二，紅油十字帕、竿袋、魚鉤帕數同上，兜地帕一，圍裙一。

translations.literal: Also supplied: a gold-over-silver canopy top; six dragon heads; four ridge-running dragons; six ridge-running cloud medallions; forty applied-tracery dragons; thirty applied-tracery cloud medallions; eight bell pendants; four seated dragons on plug pins; a full set of ring ropes; one pair of cymbal screens; four panels of sandalwood tortoise-back red gauze windows; one red silk-bordered red-bamboo door curtain; a full drip-edge set; two viewing-window curtains; one vermilion-lacquered rattan-faced chair with bright gold carved wooden dragon head; one footrest; one red cord knot; two vermilion-lacquered small tables; a full set of red silk cushions; sixteen red silk-bordered shoulder and arm mats; a full set of tie straps; four gold-over-silver iron-core pole shafts; four fish hooks; one fire footrest; a full vermilion-lacquered ladder tray; two vermilion-lacquered garment boxes; two gold-plated bronze handgrip leaf-section carrying forks; two gold-plated bronze fork-head mud-dragging running boards; two gold-over-silver leaf carrying poles; four red plush flat bands; one red silk soft screen and one side curtain each; one foot-cushion mat, one back-rest seat cushion, and one stepping bed each; one red silk cross cloth; four pole bags; two fish-hook cloths; red-oiled cross cloths, pole bags, and fish-hook cloths in the same numbers; one ground-cover cloth; and one apron skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The delivery also included a gold-over-silver canopy, six dragon heads, four ridge dragons and six cloud medallions, forty applied dragon ornaments and thirty cloud medallions, eight bell pendants, four seated dragon finials, ring ropes, cymbal screens, four sandalwood tortoise-back gauze window panels, a bordered red door curtain, drip edges, two viewing curtains, a vermilion rattan chair with gilt carved dragon head, footrests and tables, red silk cushions and sixteen shoulder mats, tie straps, four gilt iron-core poles with fish hooks and a fire footrest, ladder tray and garment boxes, gilt bronze carrying forks and mud boards, two gilt carrying poles, red plush bands, soft screen and side curtain, foot and back cushions with a stepping bed, cross cloths and pole bags in both plain and red-oiled sets, a ground cloth, and an apron skirt.

sentences.zh: 大安輦。

translations.literal: The Great Peace Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Peace Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平中，為萬安太后製輿，上設行龍六。

translations.literal: During the Xianping reign of Emperor Zhenzong a palanquin was made for Empress Dowager Wan'an, with six traveling dragons set upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianping era of Emperor Zhenzong, a palanquin was built for Empress Dowager Wan'an bearing six traveling dragons.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，詔皇太后御坐簷子，名大安輦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing an edict named the empress dowager's eave-palanquin the Great Peace Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1022 an edict designated the empress dowager's eave-palanquin as the Great Peace Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，尊皇太后為太皇太后，其行幸依治平元年之制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded to the throne he honored the empress dowager as grand empress dowager; her processions followed the regulations of the first year of Zhiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong came to the throne he elevated the empress dowager to grand empress dowager, and her processions followed the Zhiping regulations of 1064.

sentences.zh: 而皇太后、皇后常出，止用副金塗銀裝白藤輿，覆以棕櫚屋，飾以鳳。

translations.literal: Yet for ordinary outings the empress dowager and empress used only the secondary white-rattan palanquin with gold-over-silver fittings, covered with a palm-thatch canopy and ornamented with phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: For routine outings, however, the empress dowager and empress used only the secondary white-rattan palanquin with gold-over-silver fittings, its palm-thatch canopy adorned with phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 輦官服同乘輿平頭輦之制。

translations.literal: The attire of palanquin officers followed the regulations for the imperial flat-topped palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin bearers dressed according to the regulations for the imperial flat-topped palanquin.

sentences.zh: 於是詔太皇太后出入所乘，如萬安太后輿，上設行龍六，製飾率有加。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered that the grand empress dowager's conveyance for going out and coming in should be like Empress Dowager Wan'an's palanquin, with six traveling dragons set upon it and ornamentation generally enhanced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required that the grand empress dowager ride a palanquin like Empress Dowager Wan'an's, with six traveling dragons and ornamentation generally enhanced.

sentences.zh: 金銅車，禮典不載，則如舊制。

translations.literal: The gilt-bronze carriage, not recorded in the ritual canon, followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The gilt-bronze carriage, which the ritual canon did not describe, continued under the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 龍興。

translations.literal: The Dragon Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The Dragon Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 皇太后所乘也。

translations.literal: This was what the empress dowager rode.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager rode in it.

sentences.zh: 東都，皇太后多垂簾，皆抑損遠嫌，不肯乘輦，止用輿而已。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital empresses dowager often ruled from behind the curtain; all restrained themselves to keep distance and avoid suspicion, refusing to ride in the imperial palanquin and using only ordinary palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital empresses dowager usually ruled from behind the curtain; mindful to keep their distance and avoid suspicion, they declined the imperial palanquin and used only ordinary palanquins.

sentences.zh: 哲宗既嗣位，尊朱貴妃為皇太妃，出入許乘簷子。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhezong succeeded to the throne he honored Consort Zhu as imperial grand consort, permitting her to ride in an eave-palanquin when going out and coming in.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhezong succeeded, Consort Zhu was honored as imperial grand consort and permitted to use an eave-palanquin on her outings.

sentences.zh: 有司請用牙魚鳳為飾，傘用青。

translations.literal: The responsible offices requested ivory fish and phoenix ornaments and a green parasol.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices proposed ivory fish-and-phoenix ornaments and a green parasol.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，太皇太后詔有司尋繹典故，於是簷子飾以龍鳳，傘用紅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou the grand empress dowager ordered the offices to search out precedents; the eave-palanquin was then ornamented with dragon and phoenix, and the parasol was red.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088 the grand empress dowager ordered the offices to review precedents; the eave-palanquin was then adorned with dragons and phoenixes and the parasol made red.

sentences.zh: 九年，君臣議改簷子為輿，上設行龍五，出入由宣德東偏門。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the court discussed changing the eave-palanquin into a palanquin with five traveling dragons set upon it, entering and leaving by the east side gate of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: In 1094 the court debated replacing the eave-palanquin with a palanquin bearing five traveling dragons, to enter and leave by the east side gate of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 哲宗以皇太后諭旨，令太妃坐六龍輿出入，進黃傘，由宣德正門。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong, on the empress dowager's instruction, ordered the grand consort to ride in a six-dragon palanquin when going out and coming in, with a yellow parasol advanced before her, entering and leaving by the main Xuande gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's instruction, Emperor Zhezong directed the grand consort to ride a six-dragon palanquin with a yellow parasol, entering and leaving by the main Xuande gate.

sentences.zh: 於是三省議，皇太妃坐龍鳳輿，傘紅黃兼用，從皇太后出入，止用紅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Three Departments deliberated: the imperial grand consort should ride in a dragon-and-phoenix palanquin; her parasol might use both red and yellow, but when accompanying the empress dowager she used only red.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments then ruled that the imperial grand consort should ride a dragon-and-phoenix palanquin; she might use red or yellow parasols, but when accompanying the empress dowager she used only red.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，禮部太常寺言：「近奉旨：『皇太后欲令皇太妃坐六龍輿，朕常思皇太妃尊奉之禮，既不敢擬隆於皇太后，又不可不逮於中宮。』

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "We have recently received the decree: 'The empress dowager wishes the imperial grand consort to ride in a six-dragon palanquin. I often consider the rites of honor due the imperial grand consort: they must neither be raised above the empress dowager nor fall short of those for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: In 1094 the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "We have received the recent decree: 'The empress dowager wishes the imperial grand consort to ride a six-dragon palanquin. I have long weighed the honors due her: they must neither exceed those of the empress dowager nor fall below those of the empress.

sentences.zh: 今參以人情，再加詳定，伏請供進龍鳳輿。」

translations.literal: We now take human sentiment into account and deliberate further in detail; we respectfully request that a dragon-and-phoenix palanquin be supplied."
translations.idiomatic: Taking popular sentiment into account as well, we have deliberated further and respectfully request that a dragon-and-phoenix palanquin be provided."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 及徽宗即位，尊太妃為聖瑞皇太妃，詔儀物除六龍輿不用，仍進龍鳳輿外，餘悉增崇焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong took the throne he honored the grand consort as the Sagely Auspicious Imperial Grand Consort; an edict ordered that among ritual objects the six-dragon palanquin was not to be used, but apart from still advancing the dragon-and-phoenix palanquin, all the rest were generally enhanced.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne he honored her as the Sagely Auspicious Imperial Grand Consort; ritual gear was upgraded across the board, though the six-dragon palanquin was withdrawn while the dragon-and-phoenix palanquin was retained.

sentences.zh: 紹興奉迎皇太后，詔造龍輿，其制：朱質，正方，金塗銀飾，四竿，竿頭螭首，赭窗紅簾，上覆以棕，加走龍六，內設黃花羅帳、裀褥、朱椅、踏子、紅羅黃羅繡巾二。

translations.literal: When welcoming the empress dowager in the Shaoxing era an edict ordered the construction of a dragon palanquin. Its specifications: vermilion material, square form, gold-over-silver ornament, four poles with hornless-dragon heads, ochre windows and red curtains, a palm covering above with six traveling dragons added, and inside yellow-flowered silk curtains, cushions and mats, vermilion chairs, footrests, and two embroidered towels of red and yellow silk.
translations.idiomatic: For the Shaoxing welcome of the empress dowager, an edict commissioned a dragon palanquin: vermilion and square, with gold-over-silver fittings, four poles topped with hornless-dragon heads, ochre windows and red curtains, a palm canopy bearing six traveling dragons, and within yellow-flowered silk curtains, cushions, vermilion chairs, footrests, and two red and yellow embroidered towels.

sentences.zh: 皇太子車輅之制。

translations.literal: Regulations for the crown prince's chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing the crown prince's chariots.

sentences.zh: 唐制三等：一曰金輅，二曰軺車，三曰四望車。

translations.literal: Under the Tang system there were three grades: first, the Golden Chariot; second, the Light Carriage; third, the Four-Views Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang regulations there were three grades: the Golden Chariot, the Light Carriage, and the Four-Views Carriage.

sentences.zh: 太宗至道初，真宗為皇太子，謁太廟，乘金輅，常朝則乘馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao reign of Emperor Taizong, when Zhenzong was crown prince, he paid homage at the Imperial Ancestral Temple in the Golden Chariot but rode a horse for ordinary court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao era, when Zhenzong was crown prince, he rode the Golden Chariot to the Imperial Ancestral Temple but used a horse for routine court audiences.

sentences.zh: 真宗天禧中，仁宗為皇太子，亦同此制。

translations.literal: During the Tianxi reign of Emperor Zhenzong, when Renzong was crown prince, the same regulations applied.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhenzong's Tianxi reign, when Renzong was crown prince, the same practice held.

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和三年，議禮局上皇太子車輅之制：金輅，赤質，金飾諸末。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Zhenghe reign of Emperor Huizong the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual presented the regulations for the crown prince's chariots: the Golden Chariot was of red material with gold ornament on all extremities.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual submitted crown-prince chariot regulations: the Golden Chariot was red-bodied with gilt extremities.

sentences.zh: 重較，箱畫苣文鳥獸；

translations.literal: double side-panels; the box painted with aster patterns, birds, and beasts;
translations.idiomatic: With double side-panels and a box painted with aster motifs, birds, and beasts;

sentences.zh: 黃屋，伏鹿軾，龍輈，金鳳一在軾前。

translations.literal: a yellow canopy, a recumbent-deer front rail, a dragon-patterned shaft brace, and one gilt phoenix before the front rail.
translations.idiomatic: a yellow canopy, a recumbent-deer front rail, a dragon-patterned shaft brace, and a gilt phoenix mounted before the front rail.

sentences.zh: 設障塵。

translations.literal: A dust screen was set up.
translations.idiomatic: It carried a dust screen.

sentences.zh: 朱蓋黃裏。

translations.literal: The canopy was vermilion outside and yellow within.
translations.idiomatic: Its canopy was vermilion outside and yellow within.

sentences.zh: 輪畫朱牙。

translations.literal: The wheels were painted with vermilion spokes.
translations.idiomatic: The wheels were painted with vermilion spokes.

sentences.zh: 左建旂，九旒，右載闟戟。

translations.literal: On the left a banner with nine tassels was erected; on the right a halberd of office was mounted.
translations.idiomatic: On the left it bore a nine-tasseled banner; on the right a ceremonial halberd was mounted.

sentences.zh: 旂首金龍頭，銜結綬及鈴綏。

translations.literal: The banner head was a gilt dragon head holding knotted ribbons and bell tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The banner head was a gilt dragon holding knotted ribbons and bell tassels.

sentences.zh: 八鸞在衡，二鈴在軾。

translations.literal: Eight phoenix bells hung on the crossbar; two bells on the front rail.
translations.idiomatic: Eight phoenix bells hung on the crossbar and two on the front rail.

sentences.zh: 駕赤騮四，金鍐方釳，插翟尾，鏤錫，鞶纓九就。

translations.literal: Four chestnut bays drew it, with gilt square bits, inserted pheasant tail plumes, carved forehead plates, and belly bands with nine tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Four chestnut bays drew it, fitted with gilt square bits, inserted pheasant tail plumes, carved forehead plates, and nine-tasseled belly bands.

sentences.zh: 從祀、謁太廟、納妃則供之。

translations.literal: It was provided for accompanying sacrifices, paying homage at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and receiving a consort.
translations.idiomatic: It was used when accompanying sacrifices, visiting the Imperial Ancestral Temple, or taking a consort.

sentences.zh: 軺車，金飾諸末，紫油通幰，紫油纁朱裏，駕馬一。

translations.literal: The Light Carriage had gold ornament on all extremities, a full purple-oil canopy, purple oil with light red and vermilion lining, and was drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Light Carriage was gilt at every extremity, with a full purple-oil canopy lined in light red and vermilion, drawn by a single horse.

sentences.zh: 四望車，金飾諸末，青油通幰，青油纁朱裏，朱絲絡網，駕馬一。

translations.literal: The Four-Views Carriage had gold ornament on all extremities, a full green-oil canopy, green oil with light red and vermilion lining, a vermilion silk net panel, and was drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Four-Views Carriage was gilt at every extremity, with a full green-oil canopy lined in light red and vermilion, a vermilion silk net panel, and a single horse.

sentences.zh: 軺車、四望車以次列於鹵簿仗內。

translations.literal: The Light Carriage and Four-Views Carriage were arrayed in descending order within the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Light and Four-Views carriages were ranked in order within the ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃，則有厭翟車，駕以三馬。

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort had a Fulfilled Pheasant carriage drawn by three horses.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort used a Fulfilled Pheasant carriage drawn by three horses.

sentences.zh: 出入亦乘簷子，中興簡儉，惟用藤簷子，頂梁、舁杠皆飾以玄漆，四角刻獸形，素藤織花為麵，如政和之制。

translations.literal: For going out and coming in she also rode in an eave-palanquin; after the Restoration, in frugality, only a rattan eave-palanquin was used — top beam and carrying poles all ornamented with black lacquer, beast shapes carved at the four corners, plain rattan woven with flowers as the facing, as in the Zhenghe regulations.
translations.idiomatic: She also used an eave-palanquin on outings; after the Restoration, in the spirit of austerity, only a rattan eave-palanquin was used, its top beam and poles finished in black lacquer, beast shapes carved at the corners, and plain rattan woven with floral patterns as in the Zhenghe design.

sentences.zh: 親王群臣車輅之制。

translations.literal: Regulations for the chariots of imperial princes and the court.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing the chariots of imperial princes and officials.

sentences.zh: 唐制有四：一曰象輅，親五及一品乘之；

translations.literal: Under the Tang system there were four kinds: first, the Ivory Chariot, ridden by those of the fifth degree of kinship and first rank;
translations.idiomatic: Tang regulations recognized four types: the Ivory Chariot, for kin of the fifth degree and first-rank officials;

sentences.zh: 二曰革輅，二品、三品乘之；

translations.literal: second, the Leather Chariot, ridden by second- and third-rank officials;
translations.idiomatic: the Leather Chariot, for second- and third-rank officials;

sentences.zh: 三曰木輅，四品乘之；

translations.literal: third, the Wooden Chariot, ridden by fourth-rank officials;
translations.idiomatic: the Wooden Chariot, for fourth-rank officials;

sentences.zh: 四曰軺車，五品乘之。

translations.literal: fourth, the Light Carriage, ridden by fifth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: and the Light Carriage, for fifth-rank officials.

sentences.zh: 宋親王、一品、二品奉使及葬，並給革輅，製同乘輿之副，惟改龍飾為螭。

translations.literal: In the Song, imperial princes, first- and second-rank officials on diplomatic missions or at funerals were all provided with Leather Chariots, made like the secondary imperial chariot but with dragon ornament changed to hornless dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, imperial princes and first- and second-rank officials on missions or at funerals received Leather Chariots modeled on the secondary imperial chariot, but with dragon ornament replaced by hornless dragons.

sentences.zh: 六引內三品以上乘革車，赤質，製如進賢車，無案，駕四赤馬，駕士二十五人。

translations.literal: Within the Six Escorts, those of third rank and above rode in leather carriages of red material, made like the Advancement-of-Talent carriage without a writing desk, drawn by four chestnut horses with twenty-five attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Six Escorts, officials of third rank and above rode red leather carriages modeled on the Advancement-of-Talent carriage but without a writing desk, drawn by four chestnut horses with twenty-five attendants.

sentences.zh: 其緋幰衣、絡帶、旗戟、綢杠繡文：司徒以瑞馬，京牧以隼，御史大夫以獬豸，兵部尚書以虎，太常卿以鳳，駕士衣亦同。

translations.literal: Their scarlet canopy robes, net belts, banner halberds, and silk pole embroidery were: for the Minister of Education, auspicious horses; for the Metropolitan Governor, falcons; for the Censor-in-Chief, the unicorn-beast; for the Minister of War, tigers; for the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, phoenixes — and the attendants' garments matched.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet canopy robes, net belts, banners, and silk pole embroidery varied by office: auspicious horses for the Minister of Education, falcons for the Metropolitan Governor, the unicorn-beast for the Censor-in-Chief, tigers for the Minister of War, phoenixes for the Director of Imperial Sacrifices — and the attendants' dress matched.

sentences.zh: 縣令乘軺車，黑質，兩壁紗窗，一轅，金銅飾，紫幰衣、絡帶並繡雉銜瑞草，駕二馬，駕士十八人。

translations.literal: County magistrates rode in Light Carriages of black material with gauze windows on both sides, one shaft, gilt-bronze ornament, purple canopy robes and net belts all embroidered with pheasants holding auspicious plants, drawn by two horses with eighteen attendants.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates used black Light Carriages with gauze-paneled sides, a single shaft, gilt-bronze fittings, purple canopies and belts embroidered with pheasants bearing auspicious plants, two horses, and eighteen attendants.

sentences.zh: 百官常朝皆乘馬。

translations.literal: For ordinary court audiences all officials rode horses.
translations.idiomatic: For routine court audiences all officials rode on horseback.

sentences.zh: 真宗大中祥符四年，知樞密院事王欽若言：「王公車輅上並用龍裝，乞下有司檢定制度。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu of Emperor Zhenzong, Wang Qinruo, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, said: "Princes and nobles' chariots all use dragon ornament on top; we request that the responsible offices examine and fix the regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In 1011 Wang Qinruo, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, reported: "Princely and noble chariots all bear dragon ornament; we ask that the responsible offices review the regulations."

sentences.zh: 詔下太常禮院詳定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office for detailed review.

sentences.zh: 本院言：「按《鹵簿令》，王公已下，象輅以象飾諸末，朱班輪，八鸞在衡，左建旂畫龍，一升一降，右載闟戟。

translations.literal: " That office reported: "According to the Regulations for the Guard of Honor, for princes and nobles of rank and below, the Ivory Chariot had ivory ornament on all extremities, vermilion-spoked wheels, eight phoenix bells on the crossbar, a banner erected on the left painted with a dragon ascending and descending, and a ceremonial halberd mounted on the right.
translations.idiomatic: " The office replied: "Under the Regulations for the Guard of Honor, princes and nobles of rank and below used Ivory Chariots with ivory fittings, vermilion-spoked wheels, eight phoenix bells on the crossbar, a left banner painted with a dragon rising and falling, and a ceremonial halberd on the right.

sentences.zh: 革略以革飾諸末，左建旃，餘同象輅。

translations.literal: The Leather Chariot had leather ornament on all extremities, with a pennant erected on the left; the rest as on the Ivory Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Leather Chariot had leather fittings and a pennant on the left; otherwise it matched the Ivory Chariot.

sentences.zh: 木輅以漆飾之，餘同革輅。

translations.literal: The Wooden Chariot was ornamented with lacquer; the rest as on the Leather Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Wooden Chariot was lacquered; otherwise it matched the Leather Chariot.

sentences.zh: 軺車，曲壁，青幰碧裏。

translations.literal: The Light Carriage had curved sides, a green canopy, and blue lining.
translations.idiomatic: The Light Carriage had curved sides, a green canopy, and blue lining.

sentences.zh: 諸輅皆朱質，朱蓋，朱旂旃，一品九旒，二品八旒，三品七旒，四品六旒，其鞶纓如之。」

translations.literal: All chariots were of vermilion material with vermilion canopies and vermilion banners and pennants: first rank nine tassels, second rank eight, third rank seven, fourth rank six — and the belly bands and tassels matched accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: All chariots were vermilion-bodied with vermilion canopies, banners, and pennants: first rank bore nine tassels, second eight, third seven, fourth six, with belly bands to match."

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐三年，詳定禮文所言：「《鹵簿記》公卿奉引：第一開封令，乘軺車；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng of Emperor Shenzong, the Deliberation on Ritual Texts reported: "According to the Record of the Guard of Honor, for princes and nobles leading the procession: first, the Metropolitan Magistrate, riding in a Light Carriage;
translations.idiomatic: In 1080 the Deliberation on Ritual Texts noted: "The Record of the Guard of Honor lists princes and nobles leading the procession: first the Metropolitan Magistrate in a Light Carriage;

sentences.zh: 次開封牧，隼旗；

translations.literal: next, the Metropolitan Governor, with a falcon banner;
translations.idiomatic: next the Metropolitan Governor with a falcon banner;

sentences.zh: 次太常卿，鳳旗；

translations.literal: next, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices, with a phoenix banner;
translations.idiomatic: next the Director of Imperial Sacrifices with a phoenix banner;

sentences.zh: 次司徒，瑞馬旗；

translations.literal: next, the Minister of Education, with an auspicious-horse banner;
translations.idiomatic: next the Minister of Education with an auspicious-horse banner;

sentences.zh: 次御史大夫，獬豸旗；

translations.literal: next, the Censor-in-Chief, with a unicorn-beast banner;
translations.idiomatic: next the Censor-in-Chief with a unicorn-beast banner;

sentences.zh: 次兵部尚書，虎旗，而乘革車。

translations.literal: next, the Minister of War, with a tiger banner, yet riding in a leather carriage.
translations.idiomatic: next the Minister of War with a tiger banner, though riding a leather carriage.

sentences.zh: 考之非是。

translations.literal: On examination this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: This arrangement does not hold up on examination.

sentences.zh: 謹按《周禮》巾車職曰：『孤乘夏篆，卿乘夏縵，大夫乘墨車。』

translations.literal: We respectfully note that the Rites of Zhou, Office of the Chariot Master, states: 'A feudal lord rides in a Summer-Engraved carriage, a minister in a Summer-Painted carriage, a grand master in an Ink carriage.'
translations.idiomatic: We note that the Rites of Zhou, Office of the Chariot Master, states: 'A feudal lord rides a Summer-Engraved carriage, a minister a Summer-Painted carriage, and a grand master an Ink carriage.'

sentences.zh: 司常職曰：『孤、卿建旃，大夫建物。』

translations.literal: The Office of the Banner Master states: 'Feudal lords and ministers erect pennants; grand masters erect emblems.'
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Banner Master adds: 'Feudal lords and ministers raise pennants; grand masters raise emblems.'

sentences.zh: 請公卿已下奉引，先開封令，乘墨車建物；

translations.literal: We request that for princes and nobles of rank and below leading the procession, first the Metropolitan Magistrate ride in an Ink carriage and erect an emblem;
translations.idiomatic: We propose that when princes and nobles lead the procession, the Metropolitan Magistrate go first in an Ink carriage bearing an emblem;

sentences.zh: 次開封牧，乘墨車建旗；

translations.literal: next the Metropolitan Governor ride in an Ink carriage and erect a banner;
translations.idiomatic: next the Metropolitan Governor in an Ink carriage bearing a banner;

sentences.zh: 太常卿、御史大夫、兵部尚書乘夏縵，司徒乘夏篆，並建旃。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of War ride in Summer-Painted carriages; the Minister of Education rides in a Summer-Engraved carriage — all erecting pennants.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of War should ride Summer-Painted carriages; the Minister of Education a Summer-Engraved carriage — all bearing pennants.

sentences.zh: 所以參備九旗之制。」

translations.literal: Thus the regulations for the nine banners are fully provided."
translations.idiomatic: This would complete the arrangement of the nine banners."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 政和議禮局上王公以下車製：象輅以象飾諸末，朱班輪，八鸞在衡，左建旗，右載闟戟，駕馬四，親王昏則用之。

translations.literal: The Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual in the Zhenghe era presented regulations for chariots of princes and nobles of rank and below: the Ivory Chariot had ivory ornament on all extremities, vermilion-spoked wheels, eight phoenix bells on the crossbar, a banner erected on the left, a ceremonial halberd mounted on the right, four horses — used by imperial princes at marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe era the Bureau for Deliberation on Ritual submitted chariot regulations for princes and nobles: the Ivory Chariot had ivory fittings, vermilion spokes, eight phoenix bells, a left banner, a ceremonial halberd on the right, and four horses — for imperial princes at marriage.

sentences.zh: 革車，赤質，載闟戟，緋羅繡輪衣、簾、旗、韜杠、絡帶，駕赤馬四。

translations.literal: The leather carriage was of red material, bore a ceremonial halberd, and had scarlet silk embroidered wheel covers, curtains, banners, wrapped poles, and net belts; four chestnut horses drew it.
translations.idiomatic: The leather carriage was red-bodied, bore a ceremonial halberd, and carried scarlet embroidered wheel covers, curtains, banners, wrapped poles, and net belts, drawn by four chestnut horses.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿六引，法駕鹵簿三引，開封牧第乘之。

translations.literal: For the full imperial guard of honor with six escorts and the statutory guard with three escorts, the Metropolitan Governor rode it in the corresponding position.
translations.idiomatic: In the full six-escort guard and the statutory three-escort guard, the Metropolitan Governor rode it in the appropriate position.

sentences.zh: 王公、一品、二品、三品備鹵簿，皆供革車一乘。

translations.literal: Princes, first-, second-, and third-rank officials with full guards of honor were each provided one leather carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and first-, second-, and third-rank officials with full ceremonial guards each received one leather carriage.

sentences.zh: 其輪衣、簾、旗、韜杠、絡帶繡文：開封牧以隼，大司樂以鳳，少傅以瑞馬，御史大夫以獬豸，兵部尚書以虎。

translations.literal: Embroidery on wheel covers, curtains, banners, wrapped poles, and net belts was: falcon for the Metropolitan Governor, phoenix for the Director of Music, auspicious horse for the Junior Tutor, unicorn-beast for the Censor-in-Chief, tiger for the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Wheel covers, curtains, banners, poles, and belts were embroidered accordingly: falcons for the Metropolitan Governor, phoenixes for the Director of Music, auspicious horses for the Junior Tutor, the unicorn-beast for the Censor-in-Chief, tigers for the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 軺車，黑質，紫幰衣、絡帶並繡雉，施紅錦簾，香爐、香寶結帶，駕赤馬二。

translations.literal: The Light Carriage was of black material, with purple canopy robes and net belts all embroidered with pheasants, red brocade curtains hung, incense censers and boxes tied with ribbons, drawn by two chestnut horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Light Carriage was black-bodied, with purple canopies and belts embroidered with pheasants, red brocade curtains, censers and incense boxes on ribbon ties, and two chestnut horses.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿內第一引官縣令乘之，駕馬皆有銅麵，插羽，鞶纓，攀胸鈴拂，緋絹屜，紅錦包尾。

translations.literal: Within the guard of honor the first escort official, the county magistrate, rode in it; all harness horses had bronze face plates, inserted feathers, belly bands and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, scarlet silk knee covers, and red brocade tail wrappers.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate, first escort within the ceremonial guard, used it; every horse wore bronze brow plates, feather inserts, belly bands and tassels, chest bells and whiskers, scarlet knee covers, and red brocade tail wrappers.

sentences.zh: 六年，禮制局言：

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Bureau of Ritual Regulations reported:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Bureau of Ritual Regulations reported:

sentences.zh: 大觀中，用大司樂代太常卿為第三引，蓋以大司樂掌鼓吹之事。

translations.literal: During the Daguang era the Director of Music replaced the Director of Imperial Sacrifices as the third escort, because the Director of Music supervised wind and percussion music.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daguang era the Director of Music replaced the Director of Imperial Sacrifices as third escort, since he supervised wind and percussion.

sentences.zh: 夫禮樂之官，宗伯為長，宜改用禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Among ritual and music offices the Minister of Rites is chief; the Minister of Rites should be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Among ritual and music offices the Minister of Rites ranks highest; he should take this role instead.

sentences.zh: 又第四引司徒，即用地官之長，自漢以來為三公。

translations.literal: The fourth escort, the Minister of Education, is head of the Earth Offices and has ranked among the Three Excellencies since Han times.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth escort, the Minister of Education, heads the Earth Offices and has been one of the Three Excellencies since Han times.

sentences.zh: 朝廷近改司徒為少傅，然六引司徒乃地官之事，宜改用戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The court recently changed the Minister of Education to Junior Tutor, yet the six-escort Minister of Education concerns Earth Office affairs; the Minister of Revenue should be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: The court recently renamed the Minister of Education as Junior Tutor, but the six-escort post concerns revenue affairs; the Minister of Revenue should take it instead.

sentences.zh: 其府佐依六引諸卿例，改為僚佐，其鹵簿儀仗，依兵部尚書例給。

translations.literal: His office assistants should follow the six-escort precedent for ministers and be changed to staff assistants; his guard of honor and insignia should be provided as for the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His staff should follow the six-escort precedent for ministers, and his ceremonial guard should match that of the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 古之諸侯出封於外，同姓錫以金輅，異姓錫以象輅。

translations.literal: When ancient feudal lords were enfeoffed outside, those of the same surname were granted a Golden Chariot, those of different surnames an Ivory Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: When ancient feudal lords were enfeoffed abroad, kinsmen received a Golden Chariot and non-kin an Ivory Chariot.

sentences.zh: 蓋出而製節，則遠君而其道伸；

translations.literal: For when going out to establish regulations, one is far from the ruler and one's authority extends;
translations.idiomatic: Going out to govern, one stood far from the ruler and one's authority extended;

sentences.zh: 入而謹度，則近君而其勢屈。

translations.literal: when entering and observing restraint, one is near the ruler and one's power is bent.
translations.idiomatic: returning to court, one stood near the ruler and one's stature was humbled.

sentences.zh: 故其入覲，則不敢乘金輅、象輅，以同於王，當自降而乘墨車也。

translations.literal: Therefore when coming to audience they dared not ride the Golden or Ivory Chariot, equaling the king, but should lower themselves and ride the Ink carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Thus at audience they did not ride the Golden or Ivory Chariot, which would equal the king's, but humbly used the Ink carriage.

sentences.zh: 若公侯采地在天子縣內者，則為都鄙之長，《大司馬》所謂「師都建旃「是矣。

translations.literal: If a duke or marquis's fief lay within the Son of Heaven's district, he was chief of the capital outskirts — as the Grand Marshal says, 'the capital outskirts erect pennants.
translations.idiomatic: If a duke or marquis held a fief within the royal domain, he was chief of the capital outskirts — 'the capital outskirts erect pennants,' as the Grand Marshal says.

sentences.zh: 今開封牧列職於朝，與御史大夫同謂之卿可也，其在《周官》，則卿大夫之職是矣；

translations.literal: Today the Metropolitan Governor holds court rank and may be called a minister like the Censor-in-Chief; in the Zhou Offices this is the office of minister and grand master;
translations.idiomatic: Today the Metropolitan Governor holds court rank and may be styled a minister like the Censor-in-Chief; in the Zhou Offices this was a ministerial or grand-master post;

sentences.zh: 又無金輅、象輅之錫，而乃比於古之諸侯入覲而乘墨車，可乎？

translations.literal: yet he has received no grant of Golden or Ivory Chariot — can he be compared to ancient feudal lords coming to audience and riding the Ink carriage?
translations.idiomatic: yet he has received no Golden or Ivory Chariot — is it fitting to compare him to feudal lords at audience riding the Ink carriage?

sentences.zh: 成周上公九命，車旗以九為節，故建常九斿；

translations.literal: In the Chengzhou era a senior duke of nine commands took nine as the measure for chariot and banner, hence a standard banner of nine tassels;
translations.idiomatic: In the Chengzhou era a senior duke of nine commands used nine as the measure for chariot and banner, hence a nine-tasseled standard;

sentences.zh: 侯、伯七命，車旗以七為節，故建常七斿；

translations.literal: marquis and earl of seven commands took seven as the measure, hence seven tassels;
translations.idiomatic: marquises and earls of seven commands used seven, hence seven tassels;

sentences.zh: 子、男五命，車旗以五為節，故建常五斿；

translations.literal: viscount and baron of five commands took five as the measure, hence five tassels;
translations.idiomatic: viscounts and barons of five commands used five, hence five tassels;

sentences.zh: 其卿六命，其大夫四命，車旗亦各氐其命之數。

translations.literal: ministers of six commands and grand masters of four commands likewise reduced chariot and banner to their command numbers.
translations.idiomatic: ministers of six commands and grand masters of four likewise scaled chariot and banner to their rank.

sentences.zh: 則卿之建旃當用六斿，大夫建物當用四斿，至於三斿則上士所建也。

translations.literal: Thus a minister's pennant should have six tassels, a grand master's emblem four tassels; three tassels were for senior servitors.
translations.idiomatic: A minister's pennant should bear six tassels, a grand master's emblem four; three tassels were for senior servitors.

sentences.zh: 其開封令，宜乘墨車而建物四斿；

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Magistrate should ride an Ink carriage and erect a four-tasseled emblem;
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Magistrate should ride an Ink carriage bearing a four-tasseled emblem;

sentences.zh: 開封牧、御史大夫、戶部兵部禮部尚書皆卿也，宜乘夏縵而建旃六斿。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor, Censor-in-Chief, and Ministers of Revenue, War, and Rites are all ministers; they should ride Summer-Painted carriages and erect six-tasseled pennants.
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Governor, Censor-in-Chief, and Ministers of Revenue, War, and Rites are ministers all; they should ride Summer-Painted carriages with six-tasseled pennants.

sentences.zh: 其年，詳定官蔡攸又言：

translations.literal: That year the deliberating official Cai You further reported:
translations.idiomatic: That year Cai You of the deliberating office added:

sentences.zh: 六引，開封令乘軺車居前，開封牧、大司樂、司徒、御史大夫、兵部尚書乘革車次之。

translations.literal: In the six escorts the Metropolitan Magistrate rode a Light Carriage in front; the Metropolitan Governor, Director of Music, Minister of Education, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of War rode leather carriages after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the six escorts the Metropolitan Magistrate led in a Light Carriage, followed by the Metropolitan Governor, Director of Music, Minister of Education, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of War in leather carriages.

sentences.zh: 開封牧建繡隼旗，太常卿建繡鳳旗，司徒繡瑞馬旗，御史大夫繡以獬豸，兵部尚書繡以虎，皆副之以闟戟。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor erected an embroidered falcon banner; the Director of Imperial Sacrifices an embroidered phoenix banner; the Minister of Education an auspicious-horse banner; the Censor-in-Chief embroidery of the unicorn-beast; the Minister of War embroidery of tigers — all supplemented with ceremonial halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Governor bore an embroidered falcon banner, the Director of Imperial Sacrifices a phoenix, the Minister of Education an auspicious horse, the Censor-in-Chief the unicorn-beast, the Minister of War a tiger — each with a ceremonial halberd as well.

sentences.zh: 其先後之序，所乘之車，所建之旗，揆古則不合，驗今則有戾。

translations.literal: The order of precedence, the carriages ridden, and the banners erected — measured against antiquity they do not accord, tested against the present they are at odds.
translations.idiomatic: The order of march, the carriages used, and the banners raised accord neither with antiquity nor with present practice.

sentences.zh: 且大駕之出，自漢光武時始有三引：先河南尹，次執金吾，次洛陽令，先尊而後卑也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the great imperial procession set out, from Emperor Guangwu of Han there were three escorts: first the Metropolitan Governor of Henan, next the Commandant of the Capital Garrison, next the Metropolitan Magistrate of Luoyang — the honored first, the humble after.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Guangwu of Han the great procession used three escorts: the Metropolitan Governor of Henan first, then the Commandant of the Capital Garrison, then the Metropolitan Magistrate of Luoyang — honored ranks before humble ones.

sentences.zh: 後魏亦三引：先平城令，次司隸校尉，次丞相，先卑而後尊也。

translations.literal: Later Wei also had three escorts: first the Magistrate of Pingcheng, next the Director of the Capital Inspectors, next the Chancellor — the humble first, the honored after.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei likewise used three escorts: the Magistrate of Pingcheng first, then the Director of the Capital Inspectors, then the Chancellor — humble ranks before honored ones.

sentences.zh: 唐兼用六引，五代減為三，後周復增為六。

translations.literal: Tang used both six escorts; the Five Dynasties reduced them to three; Later Zhou restored six again.
translations.idiomatic: Tang employed six escorts; the Five Dynasties cut them to three; Later Zhou restored six.

sentences.zh: 本朝因之，以開封令居前，終以兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Our dynasty followed this, placing the Metropolitan Magistrate in front and ending with the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty followed suit, with the Metropolitan Magistrate leading and the Minister of War last.

sentences.zh: 然以前為尊，則大司樂不當次令、牧；

translations.literal: Yet if precedence before is honored, the Director of Music should not follow the Magistrate and Governor;
translations.idiomatic: If front rank denotes honor, the Director of Music should not follow the Magistrate and Governor;

sentences.zh: 以後為尊，則兵部尚書不當繼御史大夫，此先後之序未正也。

translations.literal: if precedence after is honored, the Minister of War should not follow the Censor-in-Chief — thus the order of precedence is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: if rear rank denotes honor, the Minister of War should not follow the Censor-in-Chief — the order of precedence is therefore wrong.

sentences.zh: 軺車非縣令宜駕，革車非公卿宜用，是所乘之車未稱也。

translations.literal: The Light Carriage is not what a county magistrate should ride; the leather carriage is not what princes and nobles should use — thus the carriages ridden are inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: A Light Carriage ill suits a county magistrate, and a leather carriage ill suits princes and nobles — the vehicles are mismatched to rank.

sentences.zh: 鳳馬之繡，無所經見，闟戟之設，尤為訛謬，是所建之旗未宜也。

translations.literal: Embroidery of phoenix and horse is nowhere attested; the setting up of ceremonial halberds is especially erroneous — thus the banners erected are unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix-and-horse embroidery appears nowhere in the classics; mounting ceremonial halberds is especially mistaken — the banners are unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 司徒，三公論道之官，車徒非其所任，戶部主之可也。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education, among the Three Excellencies a discussant of the Way, is not charged with chariots and foot soldiers — the Minister of Revenue may preside.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education, a Three Excellency charged with discourse on the Way, does not oversee chariots and troops — the Minister of Revenue should.

sentences.zh: 奉常掌禮，司樂典樂，皆專於一事，禮樂之容，非其所兼，禮部總之宜也。

translations.literal: The Director of Constant Offerings oversees ritual; the Director of Music oversees music — each specializes in one matter and cannot combine ritual and music; the Ministry of Rites should supervise both.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Constant Offerings handles ritual and the Director of Music handles music — each has a single charge and cannot combine both; the Ministry of Rites should oversee them.

sentences.zh: 請改司徒用戶部尚書，改大司樂用禮部尚書，其僚佐儀製視兵部尚書。

translations.literal: We request that the Minister of Education be replaced by the Minister of Revenue and the Director of Music by the Minister of Rites; their staff and ceremonial provisions should follow the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Minister of Revenue replace the Minister of Education and the Minister of Rites replace the Director of Music, with staff and ceremonial gear matching the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫，位亞三少，秩從二品，又尊於六尚書。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief ranks below the Three Juniors yet holds the second rank and stands above the Six Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief ranks below the Three Juniors but holds second rank and stands above the Six Ministers.

sentences.zh: 其行，宜以兵部次令、牧，禮部、戶部又次之，終以御史大夫，則先後之序正矣。

translations.literal: In procession the Minister of War should follow the Magistrate and Governor; the Ministers of Rites and Revenue should follow again; the Censor-in-Chief should come last — then the order of precedence would be correct.
translations.idiomatic: In procession the Minister of War should follow the Magistrate and Governor, then the Ministers of Rites and Revenue, with the Censor-in-Chief last — that would set the order right.

sentences.zh: 夏篆者，篆其車而五采畫之也，夏縵則五采畫之而不篆，墨車則漆之而不畫。

translations.literal: Summer-Engraved means engraving the carriage and painting it in the five colors; Summer-Painted means painting in the five colors without engraving; Ink means lacquering without painting.
translations.idiomatic: Summer-Engraved means engraving the carriage and painting it in five colors; Summer-Painted means painting in five colors without engraving; Ink means lacquer only, without painting.

sentences.zh: 孤宜乘夏篆，象其文質之備；

translations.literal: A feudal lord should ride Summer-Engraved, symbolizing the completeness of pattern and substance;
translations.idiomatic: A feudal lord should ride Summer-Engraved, symbolizing full pattern and substance;

sentences.zh: 卿宜乘夏縵，象其文采而不足於篆。

translations.literal: a minister should ride Summer-Painted, symbolizing ornamented pattern yet falling short of engraving.
translations.idiomatic: a minister Summer-Painted, symbolizing ornament but short of full engraving.

sentences.zh: 開封令秩比大夫，開封牧古之諸侯，其乘皆宜墨車。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Magistrate's rank equals a grand master; the Metropolitan Governor is like an ancient feudal lord — both should ride Ink carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Magistrate ranks as a grand master and the Metropolitan Governor as an ancient feudal lord — both should use Ink carriages.

sentences.zh: 其駕之馬，令以三，牧以四，御史大夫以六，尚書，卿之任也，其駕亦四，則所乘之車稱矣。

translations.literal: Horses drawing them: three for the Magistrate, four for the Governor, six for the Censor-in-Chief; ministers, a minister's charge, also four — then the carriages ridden would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Harness should be three horses for the Magistrate, four for the Governor, six for the Censor-in-Chief, and four for ministers — then the vehicles would match rank.

sentences.zh: 《司常》曰：「孤、卿建旃，大夫、士建物，師都建旗。」

translations.literal: The Banner Master says: 'Feudal lords and ministers erect pennants; grand masters and servitors erect emblems; the capital outskirts erect banners.'
translations.idiomatic: The Banner Master says: 'Feudal lords and ministers raise pennants; grand masters and servitors raise emblems; the capital outskirts raise banners.'

sentences.zh: 蓋通帛為旃，其色純赤；

translations.literal: For plain silk makes a pennant, its color pure red;
translations.idiomatic: Plain silk makes a pennant, pure red in color;

sentences.zh: 雜帛為物，其色赤白；

translations.literal: mixed silk makes an emblem, its color red and white;
translations.idiomatic: mixed silk makes an emblem, red and white;

sentences.zh: 物為三斿，旃亦如之。

translations.literal: an emblem has three tassels, and a pennant likewise.
translations.idiomatic: an emblem bears three tassels, and a pennant likewise.

sentences.zh: 開封令秩視大夫，故宜建以物；

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Magistrate's rank equals a grand master, so he should erect an emblem;
translations.idiomatic: The Metropolitan Magistrate ranks as a grand master and should bear an emblem;

sentences.zh: 開封牧率王畿之眾而衛上，師都之任也，故宜建以旗；

translations.literal: the Metropolitan Governor leads the masses of the royal domain to guard the sovereign — the charge of the capital outskirts — so he should erect a banner;
translations.idiomatic: the Metropolitan Governor leads the royal domain to guard the sovereign — a capital-outskirts charge — and should bear a banner;

sentences.zh: 尚書、御史大夫，古之卿也，故宜建以旃。

translations.literal: ministers and the Censor-in-Chief are ancient ministers, so they should erect pennants.
translations.idiomatic: ministers and the Censor-in-Chief are ministers of old and should bear pennants.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，禮制局言：「昨討論大駕六引，開封牧乘墨車，兵部尚書、禮部尚書、戶部尚書、御史大夫乘夏縵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Bureau of Ritual Regulations reported: "In yesterday's deliberation on the six escorts of the great imperial procession, the Metropolitan Governor rides an Ink carriage; the Ministers of War, Rites, and Revenue and the Censor-in-Chief ride Summer-Painted carriages.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Bureau of Ritual Regulations reported: "In our recent deliberation on the six escorts of the great procession, the Metropolitan Governor rides an Ink carriage and the Ministers of War, Rites, and Revenue and the Censor-in-Chief ride Summer-Painted carriages.

sentences.zh: 已經冬祀陳設訖，所有駕士衣服，尚循舊六引之制，宜行改正，況天子五輅，駕士之服，各隨其輅之色，則六引駕士之服，當亦如之。

translations.literal: The winter sacrifice display has already been set out, yet the attire of all carriage attendants still follows the old six-escort regulations and should be corrected; moreover, for the Son of Heaven's five chariots the attendants' garments each follow the color of the chariot — the six-escort attendants' garments should likewise do so.
translations.idiomatic: The winter sacrifice display is already set, yet attendants' dress still follows the old six-escort rules and should be corrected; for the Son of Heaven's five chariots, attendants dress to match each chariot's color — the six escorts should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 請墨車駕士衣皂，夏縵駕士皂質繡五色團花，於禮為稱。」

translations.literal: We request that Ink-carriage attendants wear black, and Summer-Painted attendants black garments embroidered with five-colored round floral designs — this would be ritually fitting."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Ink-carriage attendants wear black and Summer-Painted attendants black robes embroidered with five-colored round flowers — which would be ritually appropriate."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 肩輿。

translations.literal: The Shoulder Palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The Shoulder Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 神宗優待宗室老疾不能騎者，出入聽肩輿。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong showed favor to imperial clansmen who were aged or ill and could not ride, permitting them to use shoulder palanquins when going out and coming in.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong allowed aged or infirm clansmen who could not ride to use shoulder palanquins on their outings.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，太宗正司請宗室以病肩輿者，踏引、籠燭不得過兩對。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining the Directorate of the Taizong Line requested that clansmen using shoulder palanquins for illness might have no more than two pairs of foot-guides and caged candles.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072 the Directorate of the Taizong Line ruled that clansmen using shoulder palanquins for illness might have no more than two pairs of foot-guides and caged candles.

sentences.zh: 中興後，人臣無乘車之制，從祀則以馬，常朝則以轎。

translations.literal: After the Restoration officials had no regulations for riding in carriages; for accompanying sacrifices they used horses, for ordinary court audiences sedan chairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration officials had no prescribed carriages; they rode horses when accompanying sacrifices and sedan chairs for routine court audiences.

sentences.zh: 舊制，輿簷有禁。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations palanquins and eave-palanquins were restricted.
translations.idiomatic: Under earlier regulations palanquins and eave-palanquins were restricted.

sentences.zh: 中興東征西伐，以道路阻險，詔許百官乘轎，王公以下通乘之。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, with campaigns east and west and roads rugged and dangerous, an edict permitted all officials to ride sedan chairs; princes and nobles of rank and below might all use them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration, with campaigns in every direction and roads treacherous, an edict allowed all officials sedan chairs, and princes and nobles likewise.

sentences.zh: 其制：正方，飾有黃、黑二等，凸蓋無梁，以篾席為障，左右設牖，前施簾，舁以長竿二，名曰竹轎子，亦曰竹輿。

translations.literal: Its specifications: square form, ornament in yellow and black grades, a convex canopy without beams, bamboo-mat screens, windows set left and right, a curtain hung in front, borne on two long poles — called a bamboo sedan chair, also a bamboo palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: It was square, finished in yellow or black, with a convex beamless canopy, bamboo-mat screens, side windows, a front curtain, and two long carrying poles — called a bamboo sedan or bamboo palanquin.

sentences.zh: 內外命婦之車。

translations.literal: Carriages of titled women inside and outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The carriages of titled women within and outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 唐制有厭翟車、翟車、安車、白銅飾犢車，而幰網有降差。

translations.literal: The Tang system had Fulfilled Pheasant, Pheasant, and Peace carriages and a calf carriage with white-copper ornament, with graded reductions in canopy and net panels.
translations.idiomatic: Tang regulations included Fulfilled Pheasant, Pheasant, and Peace carriages and a white-copper calf carriage, with graded reductions in canopy and net panels by rank.

sentences.zh: 宋制，銀裝白藤輿簷，內命婦皇親所乘；

translations.literal: Under Song regulations, silver-fitted white-rattan palanquin eaves were ridden by titled women within the palace and imperial kin;
translations.idiomatic: Under Song rules, silver-fitted white-rattan eave-palanquins were for titled palace women and imperial kin;

sentences.zh: 白藤輿簷、金銅犢車、漆犢車，或覆以氈，或覆以棕，內外命婦通乘。

translations.literal: white-rattan palanquin eaves, gilt-bronze calf carriages, and lacquered calf carriages, sometimes covered with felt or palm — all titled women inside and outside the palace might ride them in common.
translations.idiomatic: white-rattan eave-palanquins, gilt-bronze calf carriages, and lacquered calf carriages, sometimes with felt or palm coverings — all titled women within and outside the palace could use them.

sentences.zh: 傘。

translations.literal: Parasols.
translations.idiomatic: Parasols.

sentences.zh: 人臣通用，以青絹為之。

translations.literal: Officials used them in common, made of green silk.
translations.idiomatic: Officials commonly used green silk parasols.

sentences.zh: 宋初，京城內獨親王得用。

translations.literal: Early in the Song, within the capital only imperial princes might use them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, only imperial princes within the capital might use them.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國中，宰相、樞密使始用之。

translations.literal: During the Taiping Xingguo reign of Emperor Taizong, grand councilors and commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs first began to use them.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizong's Taiping Xingguo reign, grand councilors and military commissioners first gained the privilege.

sentences.zh: 其後，近臣及內命婦出入皆用。

translations.literal: Thereafter, intimate officials and titled women within the palace all used them when going out and coming in.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter intimate officials and titled palace women used them on all outings.

sentences.zh: 真宗大中祥符五年，詔除宗室外，其餘悉禁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu of Emperor Zhenzong an edict forbade all except the imperial clan from using them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1012 Emperor Zhenzong forbade their use by all except the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 明年，復許中書、樞密院用焉。

translations.literal: The next year use was again permitted to the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs were again permitted to use them.

sentences.zh: 京城外，則庶官通用。

translations.literal: Outside the capital, ordinary officials used them in common.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital, ordinary officials used them freely.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧之制，非品官禁用青蓋，京城惟執政官及宗室許用。

translations.literal: Under the Xining regulations of Emperor Shenzong, officials without rank were forbidden green canopies; within the capital only chief councilors and the imperial clan were permitted to use them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shenzong's Xining rules, unranked officials could not use green canopies; within the capital only chief councilors and the imperial clan could.

sentences.zh: 哲宗紹聖二年，詔在京官不得用涼扇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng of Emperor Zhezong an edict forbade capital officials from using cooling fans.
translations.idiomatic: In 1095 Emperor Zhezong forbade capital officials from using cooling fans.

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和三年，以燕、越二王出入，百官不避，乃賜三接青羅傘一，紫羅大掌扇二，塗金花鞍韉，茶燎等物皆用塗金，遂為故事。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Zhenghe reign of Emperor Huizong, because the Princes of Yan and Yue went out and came in without officials yielding way, there were granted one triple-jointed green-silk parasol, two large purple-silk palm fans, gilt-flower saddle and saddle cloth, and tea braziers and the like all in gilt — thus establishing a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113, because the Princes of Yan and Yue passed through the streets without officials yielding, the court granted them one triple-jointed green-silk parasol, two large purple palm fans, gilt saddle and trappings, and gilt tea braziers and the like — establishing a lasting precedent.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔民庶享神，不得造紅黃傘、扇及彩繪，以為祀神之物。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict forbade commoners making offerings to spirits from fashioning red and yellow parasols, fans, or painted designs for use as spirit-worship objects.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict forbade commoners from making red or yellow parasols, fans, or painted regalia for spirit worship.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，又詔諸路奉天神，許用紅黃傘、扇，餘祠廟並禁。

translations.literal: Early in the Xuanhe era another edict permitted circuits worshiping the Heavenly Spirit to use red and yellow parasols and fans; all other shrines and temples were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanhe, circuits worshiping the Heavenly Spirit alone might use red and yellow parasols and fans; all other shrines were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其畫壁、塑像儀仗用龍飾者易之。

translations.literal: Where mural paintings, statues, and ritual insignia used dragon ornament, these were replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon ornament on murals, statues, and ritual gear was ordered replaced.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，初駐蹕杭州，執政張澂言：「群臣扈從兵間，權免張蓋，俟回鑾仍舊。」

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era, when the court first halted at Hangzhou, Chief Councilor Zhang Cheng said: "With ministers escorting amid warfare, parasols may be temporarily waived; when the imperial carriage returns, the old practice will resume."
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyan, when the court first halted at Hangzhou, Chief Councilor Zhang Cheng urged: "With ministers escorting the army in wartime, parasols should be waived for now and restored when the court returns north."

sentences.zh: 詔前宰相到闕，許張蓋。

translations.literal: An edict permitted former grand councilors arriving at court to use parasols.
translations.idiomatic: Former grand councilors arriving at court were permitted parasols.

sentences.zh: 鞍勒之制。

translations.literal: Regulations for saddles and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations governing saddles and bridles.

sentences.zh: 宋以賜群臣，其非賜者皆有令式，而不敢逾越焉。

translations.literal: The Song granted these to the court; what was not granted had statutory formulas, and none dared overstep them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song granted these to officials; all other cases followed statutory formulas, and none dared exceed them.

sentences.zh: 金塗銀鬧裝牡丹花校具八十兩，紫羅繡寶相花雉子方韉，油畫鞍，白銀銜鐙，以賜宰相，親王，樞密使帶使相，曾任宰相觀文殿大學士宮觀使，殿前馬軍步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Gilt-over-silver ornate peony-flower harness fittings of eighty taels, purple silk embroidered with treasure-blossom pheasant-square saddle cloth, painted saddle, white-silver bit and stirrups — granted to grand councilors, imperial princes, commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs bearing commissioner-rank, former grand councilors who were Duanming Hall grand academics or palace commissioners, and commanders-in-chief of the Palace Front cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty taels of gilt-over-silver ornate peony harness fittings, purple silk saddle cloth embroidered with treasure-blossom pheasant squares, painted saddle, and white-silver bit and stirrups went to grand councilors, imperial princes, military commissioners with commissioner rank, former grand councilors serving as Duanming grand academics or palace commissioners, and the commanders-in-chief of Palace Front cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 金塗銀鬧裝太平花校具七十兩，紫羅繡瑞草方韉，油畫鞍，陷銀銜鐙，以賜使相，樞密副使，參和政事，宣徽使，節度使，宮觀使，殿前馬軍步軍副都指揮使、都虞候。

translations.literal: Gilt-over-silver ornate peace-flower harness fittings of seventy taels, purple silk embroidered with auspicious-grass square saddle cloth, painted saddle, inlaid-silver bit and stirrups — granted to commissioner-rank officials, vice-commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, participants in state affairs, commissioners of the Palace Intendant, military governors, palace commissioners, and vice commanders-in-chief and chief inspectors of the Palace Front cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy taels of gilt-over-silver ornate peace-flower harness fittings, purple silk saddle cloth embroidered with auspicious grass, painted saddle, and inlaid-silver bit and stirrups went to commissioner-rank officials, vice military commissioners, participants in state affairs, palace intendant commissioners, military governors, palace commissioners, and vice commanders and chief inspectors of Palace Front forces.

sentences.zh: 〈（四廂都指揮使，韉以紫羅剜花。）〉

translations.literal: (For commanders of the four wings, saddle cloth of purple silk cutwork.)
translations.idiomatic: (For commanders of the four wings, saddle cloth of purple silk cutwork.)

sentences.zh: 若出使，則加紅犛牛纓，金塗銀鈸。

translations.literal: When going on mission, a red yak-hair tassel and gilt-over-silver cymbals were added.
translations.idiomatic: On diplomatic missions a red yak-hair tassel and gilt-over-silver cymbals were added.

sentences.zh: 使相在外，加紅織成鞍復。

translations.literal: Commissioner-rank officials abroad added a red brocade saddle cover.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner-rank officials serving abroad added a red brocade saddle cover.

sentences.zh: 〈（步軍都虞候以上賜帶甲馬者，加紅皮鞦轡校具七十兩，青氈圓韉，陷銀銜鐙。）〉

translations.literal: (For infantry chief inspectors and above granted armored horses, add red-leather whip-bridle fittings of seventy taels, blue felt round saddle cloth, and inlaid-silver bit and stirrups.)
translations.idiomatic: (For infantry chief inspectors and above granted armored horses, add seventy taels of red-leather whip-bridle fittings, blue felt round saddle cloth, and inlaid-silver bit and stirrups.)

sentences.zh: 金塗銀鬧裝麻葉校具五十兩，紫羅剜花方韉，油畫鞍，陷銀銜鐙，以賜三司使，觀文殿學士，資政殿大學士，翰林學士承旨，翰林學士，資政殿、端明殿、翰林侍讀侍講，龍圖、天章、寶文閣、樞密直學士，御史中丞，兩使留後，觀察、防禦使，軍廂都指揮使。
