translations.literal: Gilt-over-silver ornate hemp-leaf harness fittings of fifty taels, purple silk cutwork square saddle cloth, painted saddle, inlaid-silver bit and stirrups — granted to the Three Departments commissioner, Duanming Hall academician, Zizheng Hall grand academician, Hanlin academician ex officio, Hanlin academician, Zizheng and Duanming hall readers and lecturers, Longtu, Tianzhang, and Baowen pavilion and Bureau of Military Affairs direct academicians, vice censor-in-chief, two-commissioner military deputies, observation and defense commissioners, and wing commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty taels of gilt-over-silver ornate hemp-leaf harness fittings, purple silk cutwork saddle cloth, painted saddle, and inlaid-silver bit and stirrups went to the Three Departments commissioner, Duanming and Zizheng academics, Hanlin academicians, readers and lecturers, pavilion and military direct academicians, the vice censor-in-chief, military deputies, observation and defense commissioners, and wing commanders.

sentences.zh: 〈（軍廂都指揮使初出授團練使、刺史者，賜亦同。

translations.literal: (For wing commanders-in-chief first appointed regimental trainers or prefects, the grant is the same.
translations.idiomatic: (Wing commanders first appointed regimental trainers or prefects received the same grant.)

sentences.zh: 曾任中書、樞密院後為學士、中丞者，七十兩，韉以繡瑞草。）〉

translations.literal: for those who served in the Secretariat or Bureau of Military Affairs and later became academicians or vice censor-in-chief, seventy taels, saddle cloth embroidered with auspicious grass.)
translations.idiomatic: Those who had served in the Secretariat or Bureau of Military Affairs and later became academicians or vice censor-in-chief received seventy taels with saddle cloth embroidered with auspicious grass.)

sentences.zh: 見任中書、樞密院、宣徽使、使相、節度使出使，曾任中書、樞密院充諸路都總管、安撫使，朝辭日，賜亦如之。

translations.literal: Incumbent Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Palace Intendant, commissioner-rank, and military governor envoys, and former Secretariat or Bureau of Military Affairs officials serving as circuit grand marshals or pacification commissioners — on the day of court farewell the grant was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Incumbent Secretariat, military bureau, palace intendant, commissioner-rank, and military governor envoys, and former officials of those offices serving as circuit grand marshals or pacification commissioners received the same grant on their court farewell day.

sentences.zh: 金塗銀三環寶相花校具二十五兩，紫羅圓韉，烏漆鞍，銜鐙，以賜團練使、刺史。

translations.literal: Gilt-over-silver triple-ring treasure-blossom harness fittings of twenty-five taels, purple silk round saddle cloth, black-lacquer saddle, bit and stirrups — granted to regimental trainers and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five taels of gilt-over-silver triple-ring treasure-blossom harness fittings, purple round saddle cloth, black-lacquer saddle, and bit and stirrups went to regimental trainers and prefects.

sentences.zh: 金塗銀促結洛州花校具三十兩，紫羅圓韉，以賜諸路承受。

translations.literal: Gilt-over-silver quick-knot Luozhou-flower harness fittings of thirty taels, purple silk round saddle cloth — granted to circuit receivers.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty taels of gilt-over-silver quick-knot Luozhou-flower harness fittings and purple round saddle cloth went to circuit receivers.

sentences.zh: 白成十五兩，以賜諸王宮僚、翰林侍讀侍書；

translations.literal: White fittings of fifteen taels — granted to palace staff of imperial princes and Hanlin readers and calligraphers;
translations.idiomatic: White fittings of fifteen taels went to princes' palace staff and Hanlin readers and calligraphers;

sentences.zh: 金塗銀寶相花校具四十兩，蠻雲校具十五兩，以賜諸班押班、殿前指揮使以上；

translations.literal: Gilt-over-silver treasure-blossom harness fittings of forty taels and barbarian-cloud fittings of fifteen taels — granted to class formation leaders and Palace Front commanders and above;
translations.idiomatic: Forty taels of gilt-over-silver treasure-blossom fittings and fifteen of barbarian-cloud fittings went to class formation leaders and Palace Front commanders and above;

sentences.zh: 白成窪麵校具十二兩，以賜諸班，皆藍黃絁圓韉。

translations.literal: White concave-face fittings of twelve taels — granted to all classes; all had blue-yellow silk round saddle cloths.
translations.idiomatic: White concave-face fittings of twelve taels went to all classes, each with blue-yellow silk round saddle cloths.

sentences.zh: 其皇親婚嫁，皆給藍黃羅繡方韉，金塗銀花鞍，金塗銀校具自八十兩至十二兩，有六等。

translations.literal: For imperial kin at marriage, all were given blue-yellow silk embroidered square saddle cloths, gilt-over-silver floral saddles, and gilt-over-silver fittings from eighty taels down to twelve — six grades.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin at marriage received blue-yellow embroidered saddle cloths, gilt floral saddles, and gilt fittings from eighty down to twelve taels in six grades.

sentences.zh: 宗室女婿係親，皆賜紫羅繡瑞草方韉，校具自七十兩至五十兩，有二等。

translations.literal: Imperial-clan sons-in-law and affinal kin were all granted purple silk embroidered auspicious-grass square saddle cloths, fittings from seventy taels to fifty — two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law and affinal kin received purple saddle cloths embroidered with auspicious grass and fittings of seventy or fifty taels in two grades.

sentences.zh: 其賜契丹使，則金塗銀太平花校具七十兩，紫羅繡寶相花雉子方韉；

translations.literal: For Khitan envoys the grant was gilt-over-silver peace-flower fittings of seventy taels and purple silk embroidered treasure-blossom pheasant-square saddle cloth;
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys received seventy taels of gilt peace-flower fittings and purple saddle cloth embroidered with treasure-blossom pheasant squares;

sentences.zh: 副使則槲葉校具五十兩，紫羅繡合子地圓韉，皆油畫鞍。

translations.literal: deputy envoys received oak-leaf fittings of fifty taels and purple silk embroidered round saddle cloth with seed-pod ground — all with painted saddles.
translations.idiomatic: deputy envoys received fifty taels of oak-leaf fittings, purple round saddle cloth with seed-pod ground, and painted saddles.

sentences.zh: 〈（射弓則使銀裝，副使銀棱。）〉

translations.literal: (For shooting bows the envoy had silver fittings, the deputy silver beveled fittings.)
translations.idiomatic: (For shooting bows the envoy used silver fittings, the deputy silver beveled fittings.)

sentences.zh: 賜諸蕃進奉大使，則如刺史而用青絛韉；

translations.literal: For foreign tribute envoys the grant was like that for prefects but with green cord saddle cloth;
translations.idiomatic: Foreign tribute envoys received grants like prefects but with green cord saddle cloth;

sentences.zh: 副使則如宮僚。

translations.literal: deputies received grants like palace staff.
translations.idiomatic: deputies received grants like palace staff.

sentences.zh: 凡京官三品以上外任者，皆許馬以纓飾。

translations.literal: All capital officials of third rank and above serving outside the capital were permitted horses with tassel ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of third rank and above serving in the provinces might ornament their horses with tassels.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國七年，翰林學士承旨李昉言：「準詔詳定車服制度，請升朝官許乘銀裝絛子鞍勒，六品以下不得鬧裝，其韉皆不得刺繡、金皮飾。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo of Emperor Taizong, Hanlin academician ex officio Li Fang said: "Per the edict to deliberate on carriage and attire regulations, we request that court officials of the ascending audience be permitted silver-fitted cord saddles and bridles; those of sixth rank and below may not use ornate fittings; all saddle cloths may not be embroidered or ornamented with gold leather.
translations.idiomatic: In 982 Hanlin ex officio Li Fang reported: "Under the edict to fix carriage and dress regulations, court officials of the ascending audience should be permitted silver-fitted cord saddles and bridles; sixth rank and below may not use ornate fittings; and saddle cloths may not be embroidered or gold-leather trimmed.

sentences.zh: 餘官及工商庶人，許並乘烏漆素鞍，不得用狨毛暖坐。

translations.literal: Other officials and artisans, merchants, and commoners were all permitted black-lacquer plain saddles but might not use orangutan-fur warm seats.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials, artisans, merchants, and commoners might use plain black-lacquer saddles but not orangutan-fur warm seats.

sentences.zh: 其藍黃絛子，非宮禁不得乘。

translations.literal: Blue-yellow cord saddles might not be used outside the palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Blue-yellow cord saddles were restricted to the palace precinct.

sentences.zh: 士庶、軍校乘白皮韉勒者，悉禁斷。」

translations.literal: Gentry, commoners, and military officers riding white-leather saddle cloths and bridles were all forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Gentry, commoners, and military officers were forbidden white-leather saddle cloths and bridles."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔京朝知錄事參軍及知縣者，所乘馬並不得飾纓，後復許帶纓。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict forbade capital officials serving as record clerks or county magistrates from ornamenting their horses with tassels; later tassels were again permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year capital record clerks and county magistrates were forbidden tasseled horses; the privilege was later restored.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，詔內職諸班押班、禁軍指揮使、廂軍都虞候，並許乘銀裝絛子鞍勒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong an edict permitted inner-service class leaders, forbidden-army commanders, and wing-army chief inspectors all to ride silver-fitted cord saddles and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: In 989 inner-service class leaders, forbidden-army commanders, and wing-army chief inspectors were permitted silver-fitted cord saddles and bridles.

sentences.zh: 京官任知州、通判，許依六品朝官。

translations.literal: Capital officials serving as prefects or vice-prefects were permitted to follow sixth-rank court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials serving as prefects or vice-prefects might follow sixth-rank court rules.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平二年，西京留台上言：「留府群官、使臣乘馬，不得帶纓。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping of Emperor Zhenzong the Western Capital Remonstrance Bureau reported: "Officials and envoys of the resident capital riding horses may not wear tassels."
translations.idiomatic: In 999 the Western Capital Remonstrance Bureau reported: "Resident capital officials and envoys may not use tasseled horses."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，詔繡韉及鬧裝校具，除宗室及恩賜外，悉禁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu an edict forbade embroidered saddle cloths and ornate harness fittings except for the imperial clan and imperial grants.
translations.idiomatic: In 1012 embroidered saddle cloths and ornate harness fittings were forbidden except for the imperial clan and imperial grants.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，令兩省諫舍、宗室將軍以上，許乘狨毛暖坐，餘悉禁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi it was ordered that remonstrance officials of the two secretariats and imperial-clan generals and above might use orangutan-fur warm seats; all others were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1017 remonstrance officials of the two secretariats and imperial-clan generals and above might use orangutan-fur warm seats; all others were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 凡京官，三班已上外任者，皆許馬以纓飾。

translations.literal: All capital officials of the third class and above serving outside the capital were permitted horses with tassel ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials of the third class and above serving in the provinces might ornament their horses with tassels.

sentences.zh: 仁宗景祐三年，詔官非五品以上，毋得乘鬧裝銀鞍，其乘金塗銀裝絛子促結鞍轡者，自文武升朝官及內職、禁軍指揮使、諸班押班、廂軍都虞候、防團副使以上，聽之；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou of Emperor Renzong an edict ordered that officials below fifth rank might not ride ornate silver saddles; riding gilt-over-silver fitted cord quick-knot saddles and bridles was permitted from civil and military court officials of the ascending audience, inner-service staff, forbidden-army commanders, class formation leaders, wing-army chief inspectors, and defense and regimental vice-commissioners upward;
translations.idiomatic: In 1036 officials below fifth rank were forbidden ornate silver saddles; gilt cord quick-knot saddles and bridles were permitted from court officials, inner-service staff, forbidden-army commanders, class leaders, wing chief inspectors, and defense and regimental vice-commissioners upward;

sentences.zh: 仍毋得以藍黃為絛、白皮為韉轡。

translations.literal: and they might not use blue-yellow cords or white-leather saddle cloths and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: and they might not use blue-yellow cords or white-leather saddle cloths and bridles.

sentences.zh: 民庶止許以氈皮絁為韉。

translations.literal: Commoners were permitted only felt, leather, and coarse silk for saddle cloths.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners might use only felt, leather, or coarse silk for saddle cloths.

sentences.zh: 京官為通判以上職任者，許權依升朝例。

translations.literal: Capital officials serving as vice-prefects or in higher posts were permitted provisionally to follow the ascending-audience precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials serving as vice-prefects or higher might provisionally follow ascending-audience rules.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧間，文武升朝官、禁軍都指揮使以上，塗金銀裝盤絛促結；

translations.literal: During the Xining era of Emperor Shenzong, civil and military court officials of the ascending audience and forbidden-army commanders-in-chief and above used gilt-silver fitted coiled-cord quick-knot gear;
translations.idiomatic: During Shenzong's Xining era, ascending-audience officials and forbidden-army commanders-in-chief and above used gilt coiled-cord quick-knot gear;

sentences.zh: 五品以上，復許銀鞍鬧裝。

translations.literal: fifth rank and above were again permitted silver saddles with ornate fittings.
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank and above were again permitted ornate silver saddles.

sentences.zh: 若開花繡韉，惟恩賜乃得乘。

translations.literal: Floral embroidered saddle cloths might be ridden only when granted by imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Floral embroidered saddle cloths were permitted only by imperial grant.

sentences.zh: 餘官及民庶，仍禁銀飾。

translations.literal: Other officials and commoners were still forbidden silver ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials and commoners remained forbidden silver ornament.

sentences.zh: 舊制，諸王視宰相，用繡鞍韉。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations imperial princes were treated like grand councilors and used embroidered saddles and saddle cloths.
translations.idiomatic: Under earlier rules imperial princes, treated like grand councilors, used embroidered saddles and cloths.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，始賜金花鞍韉，諸王不施狨坐。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe gilt-floral saddles and saddle cloths were first granted; imperial princes did not use orangutan seats.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 gilt floral saddles and cloths were first granted, and imperial princes ceased using orangutan seats.

sentences.zh: 宣和末始賜，中興因之。

translations.literal: Grants began only late in Xuanhe; after the Restoration the practice continued.
translations.idiomatic: Grants began only late in Xuanhe; the practice continued after the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，重修儀製。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao ceremonial regulations were revised.
translations.idiomatic: In 1173 ceremonial regulations were revised.

sentences.zh: 權侍郎、太中大夫以上及學士、待制，經恩賜，許乘狨坐。

translations.literal: Acting vice ministers, grand masters of the palace of great rectitude and above, and academicians and court gentlemen, when granted by imperial favor, were permitted orangutan seats.
translations.idiomatic: Acting vice ministers, palace grand masters of great rectitude and above, and academicians and court gentlemen might use orangutan seats when granted by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三衙、節度使曾任執政官，亦如之。

translations.literal: The Three Bureaus and military governors who had formerly served as chief councilors were treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of the Three Bureaus and military governors who had formerly served as chief councilors were treated likewise.

sentences.zh: 先是，建炎初，駐蹕杭州，詔扈從臣僚合設狨坐者，權宜撤去。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of Jianyan when the court halted at Hangzhou, an edict ordered escorting officials who should have orangutan seats to remove them as a temporary measure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court first halted at Hangzhou in Jianyan, escorting officials were told to set aside their orangutan seats for the time being.

sentences.zh: 故事，宰執、侍從自八月朔搭坐。

translations.literal: By precedent, grand councilors and attendants set up their seats from the first day of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, grand councilors and attendants set up their warm seats from the first day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，以江、浙地燠，改為九月朔，著為例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, because the Jiang and Zhe regions were warm, this was changed to the first day of the ninth month and established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131, because Jiang and Zhe were warm, the date was moved to the first day of the ninth month and made precedent.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，乃詔三衙乘馬，賜狨坐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao an edict ordered the Three Bureaus to ride horses and granted orangutan seats.
translations.idiomatic: In 1165 the Three Bureaus were ordered to ride horses and granted orangutan seats.

sentences.zh: 門戟。

translations.literal: Gate halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Gate halberds.

sentences.zh: 木為之而無刃，門設架而列之，謂之棨戟。

translations.literal: Made of wood without blades, set on frames at the gate and arrayed — called ceremonial halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Fashioned of wood without blades and arrayed on frames at the gate, they were called ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 天子宮殿門左右各十二，應天數也。

translations.literal: At the Son of Heaven's palace gates there were twelve on each side, corresponding to the number of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's palace gates there were twelve on each side, matching the number of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宗廟門亦如之。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple gates were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple gates followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 國學、文宣王廟、武成王廟亦賜焉，惟武成王廟左右各八。

translations.literal: The National University, the Temple of King Wenxuan, and the Temple of King Wucheng were also granted them; only the Temple of King Wucheng had eight on each side.
translations.idiomatic: The National University and the temples of Kings Wenxuan and Wucheng received them as well; only the Temple of King Wucheng had eight on each side.

sentences.zh: 臣下則諸州公門設焉，私門則府第恩賜者許之。

translations.literal: For subjects they were set at public gates of the circuits; at private gates only residences granted by imperial favor were permitted them.
translations.idiomatic: For officials they stood at circuit public gates; at private gates only residences with imperial grants might display them.

sentences.zh: 太宗淳化二年，詔諸道州、府、軍、監奏乞鼓角戟槊，如令文合賜，即下三司指揮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua of Emperor Taizong an edict ordered that when circuits, prefectures, armies, and directorates memorialized requesting drums, horns, halberds, and spears, if the regulations warranted grant, the Three Departments should issue orders at once.
translations.idiomatic: In 991, when circuits, prefectures, armies, and directorates requested drums, horns, halberds, and spears, the Three Departments were to issue orders at once if regulations warranted a grant.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖四年，太常禮院言：「準批狀，詳定知廣安軍範宗古奏，本軍乞降槊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng of Emperor Renzong the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office reported: "Per the approved memorandum, in deliberating on the memorial of Fan Zonggu, prefect of Guangan Army, that army requested spears to be granted:
translations.idiomatic: In 1026 the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Ritual Office reported: "Per the approved memorandum, deliberating on Fan Zonggu's memorial as prefect of Guangan Army requesting spears:

sentences.zh: 檢會令文，京兆河南太原府、大都督府、都護門十四戟，若中都督、上都護門十二戟，下都督、諸州門各十戟，並官給。

translations.literal: checking the regulations, Jingzhao, Henan, Taiyuan prefectures, great protectorate prefectures, and protectorates had fourteen halberds at the gate; middle protectorate and upper protectorate gates twelve; lower protectorate and circuit gates ten each — all supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: regulations provided fourteen halberds for Jingzhao, Henan, Taiyuan, great protectorate prefectures, and protectorates; twelve for middle and upper protectorate gates; ten for lower protectorate and circuit gates — all government supplied.

sentences.zh: 所有軍、監門不載，伏請不行。」

translations.literal: army and directorate gates are not recorded; we respectfully request that this not be approved."
translations.idiomatic: Army and directorate gates are not listed; we respectfully ask that the request be denied."

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐之制，凡門列戟者，官司則開封、河南、應天、大名、大都督府皆十四，中都督皆十二，下都督皆十。

translations.literal: Under the Yuanfeng regulations of Emperor Shenzong, for all gates displaying halberds: government offices — Kaifeng, Henan, Yingtian, Daming, and great protectorate prefectures all fourteen; middle protectorate all twelve; lower protectorate all ten.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong's Yuanfeng rules, gates with halberds were allotted as follows: Kaifeng, Henan, Yingtian, Daming, and great protectorate prefectures fourteen; middle protectorate twelve; lower protectorate ten.

sentences.zh: 品官恩賜者，正一品十六，二品以上十四。

translations.literal: For ranked officials granted by imperial favor: first rank sixteen, second rank and above fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials with imperial grants received sixteen at first rank and fourteen at second rank and above.

sentences.zh: 中興仍舊制。

translations.literal: After the Restoration the old regulations continued.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration the old rules continued.

sentences.zh: 旌節。

translations.literal: Banners and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and insignia.

sentences.zh: 唐天寶中置，節度使受命日賜之，得以專製軍事，行即建節，府樹六纛。

translations.literal: Established in the Tianbao era of Tang; on the day a military governor received his commission it was granted, enabling exclusive control of military affairs; when traveling the insignia was displayed, and six great banners were planted at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Introduced in Tang's Tianbao era, it was granted on the day a military governor took office, giving him exclusive military authority; on campaign he displayed the insignia, and six great banners stood at his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 宋凡命節度使，有司給門旗二，龍、虎各一，旌一，節一，麾槍二，豹尾二。

translations.literal: Whenever the Song appointed a military governor, the responsible offices supplied two gate banners, one dragon and one tiger, one standard, one insignia staff, two command spears, and two leopard tails.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Song appointed a military governor, the responsible offices supplied two gate banners, one dragon and one tiger, one standard, one insignia staff, two command spears, and two leopard tails.

sentences.zh: 旗以紅繒九幅，上設耀篦、鐵鑽、髹杠、緋纛。

translations.literal: Banners used nine panels of red silk, topped with radiant finials, iron spikes, lacquered poles, and scarlet pennons.
translations.idiomatic: Banners used nine panels of red silk with radiant finials, iron spikes, lacquered poles, and scarlet pennons.

sentences.zh: 旌用塗金銅螭頭，髹杠，綢以紅繒，畫白虎，頂設髹木盤，周用塗金飾。

translations.literal: The standard used a gilt-bronze hornless-dragon head, lacquered pole, silk bound with red silk painted with a white tiger, a lacquered wooden disk at the top, and gilt ornament all around.
translations.idiomatic: The standard bore a gilt-bronze hornless-dragon head on a lacquered pole wrapped in red silk painted with a white tiger, topped by a lacquered disk with gilt trim.

sentences.zh: 節亦用髹杠，飾以金塗銅葉，上設髹圓盤三層，以紅綠裝釘為旄，並綢以紫綾復囊，又加碧油絹袋。

translations.literal: The insignia staff also used a lacquered pole ornamented with gilt-bronze leaves, three layers of lacquered round disks above, red and green studded tassels, all wrapped in purple silk double bags and further covered with a blue-oil silk pouch.
translations.idiomatic: The insignia staff used a lacquered pole with gilt-bronze leaves, three lacquered disks, red and green studded tassels, a purple silk double wrap, and a blue-oil silk pouch.

sentences.zh: 麾槍設髹木盤，綢以紫繒復囊，又加碧油絹袋。

translations.literal: Command spears had lacquered wooden disks, were wrapped in purple silk double bags, and further covered with blue-oil silk pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Command spears had lacquered disks, purple silk double wraps, and blue-oil silk pouches.

sentences.zh: 豹尾，製以赤黃布，畫豹文，並髹杠。

translations.literal: Leopard tails were made of red-yellow cloth painted with leopard patterns, all on lacquered poles.
translations.idiomatic: Leopard tails were red-yellow cloth painted with leopard patterns on lacquered poles.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧五年，詔新建節並移鎮，並降敕太常寺排比旌節，下左右金吾街仗司、騏驥院，給執擎人員、鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining of Emperor Shenzong an edict ordered that newly established commands and transfers of headquarters all receive decrees for the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to arrange banners and insignia, transmitted to the Left and Right Golden Crow Street Guard Office and the Fine-Horses Park to supply bearers, saddles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072 newly established commands and transferred headquarters received orders for the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to arrange banners and insignia, with the Golden Crow guard offices and Fine-Horses Park to supply bearers, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 中興因之。

translations.literal: After the Restoration this continued.
translations.idiomatic: After the Restoration this continued.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，表韓世忠之旗曰「忠勇」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan Han Shizhong's banner was inscribed "Loyal and Brave."
translations.idiomatic: In 1129 Han Shizhong's banner was inscribed "Loyal and Brave."

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，表岳飛之旗曰「精忠」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing Yue Fei's banner was inscribed "Utter Loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 Yue Fei's banner was inscribed "Utter Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 孝宗詔以其藩邸旌節，迎置天章閣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong ordered that the banners and insignia of his princely residence be welcomed and installed in the Tianzhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong ordered the banners and insignia of his princely residence installed in the Tianzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，光宗亦詔奉東宮旌節。

translations.literal: During Chunxi, Emperor Guangzong also ordered the Eastern Palace banners and insignia to be enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi, Emperor Guangzong likewise enshrined the Eastern Palace banners and insignia.

sentences.zh: 其後，寧宗踐祚，有司言安奉皇帝藩邸旌節，宜有推飾。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, the responsible offices said that enshrining the Retired Emperor's princely banners and insignia should receive enhanced ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, the responsible offices proposed enhanced ornament for enshrining the Retired Emperor's princely banners and insignia.

sentences.zh: 今用朱漆青地金字牌二：其一題曰「太上皇帝藩邸旌節」，其一曰「今上皇帝藩邸旌節。」

translations.literal: Now two vermilion-lacquer plaques with blue ground and gilt characters are used: one inscribed "Banners and Insignia of the Supreme Emperor's Princely Residence," the other "Banners and Insignia of the Present Emperor's Princely Residence."
translations.idiomatic: Two vermilion-lacquer plaques on blue ground with gilt characters are now used: one reading Banners and Insignia of the Supreme Emperor's Princely Residence, the other Banners and Insignia of the Present Emperor's Princely Residence."

sentences.zh: 蓋襲用元豐延安故事雲。

translations.literal: This followed the Yuanfeng precedent of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: This followed the Yuanfeng precedent of Yan'an.
